title: A six-order average assigned similar peak-excess shares to Lena and Yenisey in 31 certified years from 1980 to 2011
abstract: We tested whether a prior 97% conditional Lena share of a three-river peak excess survives an average across all six orders of breaking year matching. We used ArcticGRO daily flow at Ob, Yenisey and Lena gauges in 31 certified years from 1980 to 2011. The six-order average assigned 49.11% to Lena, 47.91% to Yenisey and 2.98% to Ob. The Lena-minus-Yenisey allocation was 51 cubic metres per second, with a conditional 97.5% three-year block interval from -150 to 241. Equal seasonal volumes also gave similar shares. A separate earlier 29-year sample had uncertain contrasts. Exact algebra shows that this rule splits pair-preservation contrasts equally between pair members. The prior order-specific result is reproduced; it is not a unique river share. Short records, selected follow-up tests, bootstrap bias, regulation and gauge error limit inference. No physical cause or coastal pulse is identified. The package gives code, all aggregate draws, source hashes, independent arithmetic checks and a figure. External raw data stay outside the package.

display.caption: Six-order mean allocations for recent and earlier certified samples. Bars give conditional 95% three-year circular block intervals. They are descriptive accounting intervals, not causal effects.
